Added AuthData(accountId, acr, amr) and ChannelResponse.authData (tool_api/Envelope.kt). ChannelService.authDataFor(channel) is null for APP, and for WEB always returns the object (accountId straight off the channel, unlike ChannelBlock's own account fields not gated on hasProvenFactor - Keycloak needs accountId the moment it's known; acr/amr come from the channel's AuthContext, null until a first proof). Wired into every response builder that already exists: ChannelService.respond (entry point + resume) and all three ToolControllerSupport response sites (abandon/applyOutcome/buildReadResponse) - so every WEB response carries it, not just the kc entry point, per the design's 'jede Antwort' requirement. The orchestrator-side half of this was already in place from bead .5: KcChannelUpsertRequest.targetAcr raises the channel's acrFloor (SessionManagementService.raiseChannelAcrFloor), and KcSelectMethodStrategy.candidatesFor already routes an already-known account through CandidateTools.forAuth(account, ctx.acrFloor, ctx) - never forIdentification - so step-up candidates are filtered by the raised floor same as the App channel's own step-up. The numeric-LoA-to-ACR-string mapping table itself is explicitly NOT orchestrator work (docs/ideen/web-keycloak-kanal.md #9: 'Teil der Konfiguration des OrchestratorAuthenticator-Plugins, nicht des Orchestrators selbst') - that lives in the mock-keycloak frontend (bead .9). Added a KcChannelIntegrationTest assertion confirming step-up candidates never include ident-fsc. Full suite green.

Mock-Keycloak frontend implemented (frontend/src/kcSigning.ts, kcApi.ts, components/MockKeycloakView.tsx, new 'Mock-Keycloak' tab in App.tsx). Backend side: MockKeycloakKeyProvider generates a fresh EC key at startup; MockKeycloakKeyController exposes it as a public JWKS (GET /mock-keycloak/.well-known/jwks.json, matching kc.peer-auth.jwks-uri) and, demo-only, the private JWK (GET /mock-keycloak/signing-key) so the frontend can sign without either side hand-copying key material. Frontend fetches the private key once, signs peer-auth assertions client-side with WebCrypto ECDSA/ES256 (same raw-signature-format fact createDpopProof in dpop.ts already relies on), and drives PATCH /kc/channels/{id} for both initial login (kcAuthSessionId anchor) and step-up (kcSessionId anchor + accountId/targetAcr inputs). Tool steps render generically from stepData.missingFields (every tool module already reports this) rather than reusing the App channel's DPoP-bound per-tool components - deliberately simpler, matches the bead's 'demo/test only' scope. authData is displayed as raw JSON, never written anywhere real.
